subject: Post-processing of Stan results to get frequentist p-values

messages.author: 11cd7b0c99a3bee8
messages.subject: Post-processing of Stan results to get frequentist p-values
parts:
Included is code to post-process Stan results to get frequentist p-values for the sampled parameters, e.g., with a likelihood-ratio test. "mcmc4" is an example with a normal distribution. "mcmc6" is an example with a negative binomial distribution.

Currently, a large part is implemented in R. However the implementation does nothing what Stan doesn't do anyway (sampling, simulation, minimization, importance sampling). Any idea how to let Stan do more of the work?

Best regards,

Christian

P.S.
The implemented algorithm is an extension of 
- Harrison, Matthew T. "Conservative hypothesis tests and confidence intervals using importance sampling." Biometrika 99.1 (2012): 57-69.
and is described in
- Bartels, Christian (2014): Efficient generic integration algorithm to determine confidence intervals and p-values for hypothesis testing. figshare. 
http://dx.doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.1054694

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Post-processing of Stan results to get frequentist p-values
parts:
I don't really know either R or hypothesis testing well enough
to help here. Just a few points:

1. Stan can only operate on one iteration at a time. Look
at the generated quantities block for making computations based
on data and params on a per-iteration basis. So as soon as you
create 'par' and operate on columns at a time, you're beyond what
you can currently do within Stan itself.

2. You have to be careful with MCMC output, as you want to
divide by n_eff, not n in any hypothesis tests due to the correlation
of the posterior.

3. You use an improper p(sigma) propto 1/sigma prior. This is OK,
as is a general improper uniform prior, as long as the posterior is
proper.

4. Renaming is error prone --- I'd suggest just making the model match
whatever you do with it other than renaming.

If you have further questions about specific Stan capabilities,
we'd be happy to help.

- Bob
